subject: Recap: API unbundling discovery w/ Horizon Health — compatibility & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@horizonhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Recap: API unbundling discovery w/ Horizon Health — compatibility & pilot next steps

Thanks again for your time today, Elena & Samir — really useful conversation. Below is a short recap so we’re aligned and have clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain points you shared:
- High per-token spend across OpenAI + Anthropic endpoints; limited visibility into token breakdowns per route.
- Latency spikes impacting live triage workflows (p95 occasionally >600ms).
- Data residency and auditability constraints for PHI-adjacent logs — procurement requires stronger retention controls and KMS integration.
- Vendor lock-in risk: reliance on proprietary function-calling/response formats that will be hard to port.

Current stack summary (what you told us):
- Generation + tool-calling: OpenAI (gpt-4o) + Anthropic for a subset of safety-critical flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3 + local vector store in Redis + Pinecone for long-term index.
- Routing: internal API gateway with per-route routing rules to each provider.
- Monitoring: Datadog traces + homegrown token-metering script.

Success criteria for Horizon Health (approx):
- Cost: ~40% reduction in per-interaction cost for ambulatory triage flows (baseline measured by tokens/session).
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for short-turn dialogues (<=512 tokens).
- Compatibility: model/function outputs must preserve structured JSON schemas for downstream parsers (no heavy post-processing).
- Security: KMS integration + SOC 2 evidence + per-tenant audit logs retained for 1 year.

Proposed immediate deliverables from Redwood (what we committed to):
1) Compatibility matrix: quick mapping (function-calling, structured output, streaming, embeddings parity) across candidate open models. (attached)
2) Pilot outline & timeline: 4‑week technical pilot scoped to triage flows with a single model variant and rollback/fallback to Anthropic if needed. (attached)
3) Pricing sketch / resource estimate for Dedicated pilot nodes and expected token cost delta.
4) SOC 2 artifacts + KMS integration notes (available by our security/PE team).

Next steps / asks from Horizon Health:
- Share a representative prompt set + 30 sample sessions (anonymized) for compatibility testing.
- Confirm legal/procurement timeline and any standard NDA (Samir).
- Availability for a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (suggest Tue/Wed).

Attachments: redwood-compatibility-matrix-v1.xlsx (compat checklist), redwood-pilot-outline-2026-11.pdf (pilot scope), redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf (SLA draft).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive once you confirm availability.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-compatibility-matrix-v1.xlsx (52KB)]

From: Elena Park <elena.park@horizonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:38:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap: API unbundling discovery w/ Horizon Health — compatibility & pilot next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear write-up. Couple of clarifications and asks from our side:
- Procurement: we’re targeting a December PO for a pilot budget but need vendor-side NDA + SOC2 docs to move legal. Samir will own this timeline.
- Compatibility: our key blockers are (1) function-calling parity (we rely on returned 'commands' that our agent executes) and (2) embeddings delta — even small shifts in vector norms break similarity thresholds.
- Success bar: in addition to your metrics, we need a fidelity metric on NLU slots (intent+entities) measured on the 30-session sample.

I can share the sample sessions tomorrow once our privacy team strips identifiers. Samir — will send an outline of procurement steps in a separate thread.

One scheduling note: Tue 12/1 10–11am ET or Wed 12/2 14–15pm ET both work for our engineers.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Clinical Platforms | Horizon Health
[Attachment: none]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@horizonhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:27:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap: API unbundling discovery w/ Horizon Health — compatibility & pilot next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Elena — that helps. Quick responses inline:
- NDA / SOC2: attaching the SOC 2 summary and NDA intake link; our security team will also provide the KMS integration note prior to the pilot start.
- Function-calling parity: in the compatibility matrix I added a "command fidelity" row — we’ll run automated callable-output checks against your sample sessions to quantify differences.
- Embeddings: we’ll include an embeddings drift test (cosine + L2 norms) and recommend a normalization layer if needed.

I’m locking Tue 12/1 10–11am ET for the technical deep-dive; invite to follow. For the pilot we propose:
- Week 0: onboarding & data transfer (anonymized samples)
- Week 1–2: compatibility tests + small A/B on triage flows (internal routing)
- Week 3: perform fidelity evaluation + cost analysis
- Week 4: review & decision gating (roll to Dedicated nodes or stop)

Deliverables at pilot close: test report (metrics), config diff for routing, and a pricing delta worksheet.

Attaching: redwood-compatibility-matrix-v1.xlsx, redwood-pilot-outline-2026-11.pdf.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pilot-outline-2026-11.pdf (140KB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizonhealth.com>

Thanks Ben — confirming NDA request and procurement timeline. Legal will need the SOC2 Type II report (not just summary) and an outline of data retention controls prior to PO. I’ve started a ticket internally — target is to clear docs by 12/10 so we can issue a PO the week of 12/13.

We’ll get the anonymized sample sessions to you by EOD Tue 12/1. For the pilot, prioritize the function-calling fidelity check and an embeddings comparison report — those will be gating for our engineers.

Samir Patel
Sr. Manager, IT Procurement | Horizon Health
